lots.title: Mechanical and Electrical (MEP) Scope of Service — Stockport Town Centre School
lots.description: Annex A.3 of the Multi-disciplinary Design Team Appointment for the Stockport Town Centre School (Project E000-25-0031). This scope annex defines the Mechanical and Electrical (MEP) consultant obligations across RIBA Plan of Work 2020 Stages 0 through 7, covering feasibility, concept design, spatial coordination, technical design, construction, handover and in-use. The appointment sits under a JCT Design & Build Contract with novation of a multi-disciplinary consultant. Services cover building services design (plumbing, above-ground drainage, mechanical and electrical engineering, service diversions and access/maintenance strategy), BIM coordination and clash detection, BREEAM contribution, compliance with the Stockport Climate Action Now (CAN) plan and Sustainable Build Standard, CDM Regulations compliance, and Disability Discrimination Act compliance. Detailed service-category breadth is enumerated in Appendix A (Mechanical and Electrical Services) and Appendix B (Life Engineering).
requirements: General description: Design and Technical Services are procuring an architecturally-led multi-disciplinary design team to develop feasibility through to concept design of a new school in a town centre location (§1.1 General).
Proposed form of building contract: JCT Design & Build Contract (§1.3 General).
Form of consultant appointment: Multi-Discipline consultant with novation (§1.4 General).
Proposed consultant payment terms: 30 days payment terms, invoices following completion of stages (§1.5 General).
Employer Liability cover required: £10,000,000 (ten million pounds) (§1.6 General).
Public Liability cover required: £10,000,000 (ten million pounds), with indemnity to principals and no annual claim-count limit (§1.7 General).
Professional Indemnity Insurance cover required: £10,000,000 (ten million pounds) per claim, no annual claim-count limit (§1.8 General).
Attend SMBC, Design, Project, Construction and other meetings as required (Core Services §1.1).

Comply with the client Organisational Information Requirements (OIR) and Employers Information Requirements (EIR) for BIM, including participating in clash detection reviews, feedback and clash-minimisation meetings (Core Services §1.2).
Supply all information required to produce a fully coordinated design alongside other Designers and agree quality of materials and standards of workmanship (Core Services §1.3).

Provide Mechanical and Electrical Services covering at minimum: Plumbing; Above Ground Drainage; all M&E engineering; Service diversions; all services outlined in the Project Briefing Document and Design Responsibility Matrix; and Access and Maintenance Strategy for all M&E elements (Core Services §1.4).
Design the Works to meet SMBC's desired objectives and outputs (Core Services §1.5).
Contribute to the Project Risk Register maintained by the client, highlighting project risks early and advising on mitigation (Core Services §1.6).
Issue Designers Risk Assessments at the conclusion of each project stage (Core Services §1.7).

Align with Stockport Council's 2019 climate emergency declaration (carbon neutral borough by 2038, council net zero by 2030) and Climate Action Now (CAN) plan. MEP survey must include high-level recommendations to meet the CAN plan and Sustainable Build Standard (Core Services §1.8).
Evaluate sustainable solutions at each stage of design (Core Services §1.9).
Support the BREEAM assessor by issuing required evidence and attending BREEAM meetings to hit the target BREEAM rating (Core Services §1.10).
Liaise with SMBC / External Project Manager and Design Team on programme maintenance, quality and progress/cost reporting, and cash flow forecasting (Core Services §1.11–1.13).
Consider and develop alternative design and material solutions that add value or deliver cost saving (Core Services §1.14).

Design the works to comply with all relevant statutory requirements, codes of practice, guidance and best practice; maintain a register of derogations and notify SMBC of any non-compliances (Core Services §1.15–1.17).
Support the process of gaining Planning Permissions, Building Control Applications and other consents (Core Services §1.18).
Ensure proposals comply with the Disability Discrimination Act (Core Services §1.19).
Make all drawn information available in PDF and DWG format (Core Services §1.20).
Issue SMBC monthly Design Progress reports and maintain a design programme (Core Services §1.21).
Maintain a Common Data Environment (CDE) for the project, details agreed with SMBC (Core Services §1.22).
Advise the client on the need for specialist advice or services (Core Services §1.23).
Visit site at regular intervals appropriate to the stage of construction to review progress, quality and compliance with the designer's design and specifications (Core Services §1.24).

RIBA Stage 0 & 1 (Strategic Definition, Preparation and Briefing): comply with RIBA Plan of Work 2020 Stages 0 and 1 and BSRIA BG6/2018 Pro-Forma 1; deliver a formal stage report; carry out site inspections; comment on physical/logistical site restrictions; work with PM/design team on initial requirements, brief, budget and programme; advise on surveys, enabling works and demolition; comply with CDM Regulations; consult statutory bodies; undertake value management (§2.1–2.13).

RIBA Stage 2 (Concept Design): comply with RIBA Stage 2 and BSRIA BG6/2018 Pro-Forma 2; deliver a formal stage report; consolidate and finalise the brief; prepare outline concept design proposals including General Arrangement Drawings (plans/elevations/sections), schedules and schematics, roof plans, large-scale details for complex areas and area/accommodation schedules; establish quality and cost management procedures; appraise all feasible design solutions; identify long-lead and specialist/proprietary components; update cost plan (§3.1–3.14).

RIBA Stage 3 (Spatial Coordination): comply with RIBA Stage 3 and BSRIA BG6/2018 Pro-Forma 3; deliver a formal stage report; develop detailed proposals including finalised grid drawings, 1:100 & 1:50 fully coordinated GA drawings, schematic drawings and schedules, full spatially-coordinated site plan, 1:100 roof layout, spatially coordinated ceiling layouts, room data sheets, and area/accommodation schedules; prepare tender documentation inputs; coordinate Builders Work, life-cycle cost and environmental assessment (§4.1–4.18).

RIBA Stage 4 (Technical Design): comply with RIBA Stage 4 and BSRIA BG6/2018 Pro-Forma 4A, 4B, 4C; deliver a formal stage report; develop technical design from detailed design per brief and cost plan; produce calculations, drawings, schedules and specifications to enable tenders; consult statutory authorities on final proposals; appraise and evaluate tenders; assist in preparing an Authority to Start Work Report; coordinate the Employer's Requirements for all construction elements (§5.1–5.12).

RIBA Stage 5 (Manufacturing and Construction): comply with RIBA Stage 5 and BSRIA BG6/2018 Pro-Forma 5; provide all construction-status details, drawings, schedules, calculations and specifications; attend site meetings and periodic visits; review/assist testing, setting-to-work, commissioning and balancing of engineering services; inspect and record defects and remedial actions; agree test certificates and statutory approvals; prepare and maintain a handover plan (§6.1–6.8).

RIBA Stage 6 & 7 (Handover, Close Out, In Use): comply with RIBA Stages 6 and 7 and BSRIA BG6/2018 Pro-Forma 6 and 7; prepare and maintain a defects administration plan; provide post-completion defect services; advise on operation and maintenance; provide drawings for the Health and Safety File; review contractor record drawings and O&M Manuals; attend Lessons Learnt workshops (§7.1–7.8).

Appendix A — Mechanical and Electrical Services: broad scope covering acoustics, HVAC, air handling, boilers, cooling towers, calorifier plant, cold/hot water services, chilled water systems, distribution mains, electrical distribution and substations, lighting fittings, environmental & sustainable engineering, kitchen/food preparation equipment, fire engineering, fire detection/alarm, firefighting, fuel gas incoming supply and distribution, heating, kitchen ventilation, incoming utility supplies, lightning protection, public address, public health/drainage (internal and external) and plumbing, radio/TV, refrigeration and cold stores, steam humidification, street/external lighting, telephone and data distribution, thermal insulation, water treatment and filtration, other specialised supply systems/plant, and vibration control in connection with services.

Appendix B — Life Engineering: advisory scope covering electrical distribution, electric lighting and power installations (including fittings), fire engineering, and fire detection and alarm services.
